problem_signature: Python pytest suites fail when editable install, test extras, pytest-xdist, and pytest version constraints are not aligned
symptoms: pytest cannot import the project test package until the repository root is visible on PYTHONPATH
tests skip xdist-dependent cases with errors such as No module named 'xdist'
newer pytest versions leave compatibility tests failing even after most tests pass
the full suite passes only after using the repository testing extra plus a compatible pytest range
root_cause: The test environment was missing the repository-declared testing extra and pytest-xdist, and latest pytest versions changed behavior expected by this older test suite. In this run, the effective setup required the local editable install with the actual extra name `.[testing]`, pytest-xdist, PYTHONPATH=/app, and pytest 6.x rather than the latest pytest release.
successful_fix: If editable install fails with git dubious ownership, first run `git config --global --add safe.directory /app`.
Install the local package with the actual repository-declared test extra, e.g. `pip install -e ".[testing]"` in this case.
Install xdist and constrain pytest to a compatible range, e.g. `pip install pytest-xdist "pytest>=5.4,<7"`, which resolved to pytest 6.2.5 in this run.
Run final verification with the repository root visible and without output truncation: `PYTHONPATH=/app pytest tests/ -v`.
verification: Full verification command `PYTHONPATH=/app pytest tests/ -v` passed with 207 tests and 1 warning.
The final Verification Bundle used `PYTHONPATH=/app pytest tests/ -v` as the test command.
anti_patterns: Assuming the latest pytest release is compatible with an older pytest plugin test suite.
Installing the editable package without the repository-specific testing extra and then chasing missing test dependencies one by one.
Treating xdist-related skips as acceptable when the repository explicitly includes pytest-xdist support.
Using `head` or `tail` on pytest output for final verification, which can hide the complete pass/fail signal.
embedding_text: Python pytest environment setup for editable packages: install the local package with the repository-declared testing extra (example: pip install -e ".[testing]"), ensure PYTHONPATH includes the repo root (/app), install pytest-xdist, and use a pytest version compatible with the suite (example: pytest>=5.4,<7 resolving to pytest 6.2.5). Symptoms include ImportError for the project test package, xdist skipped tests, and failures under pytest 7/9 due changed pytest behavior. Final verification should run the full command without head/tail truncation: PYTHONPATH=/app pytest tests/ -v.

problem_signature: Apt package installation repeatedly fails because of transient mirror/network errors or oversized install batches
symptoms: apt-get update or apt-get install reports 502, timeout, temporary failure, connection reset, or failed to fetch

root_cause: The package-manager workflow is overloaded or affected by transient mirror/network instability; installing too many unrelated packages at once makes retries expensive and failure recovery unclear.
successful_fix: Retry transient apt failures before abandoning the required dependency path
Split installation into small batches ordered by immediate need
Install the minimum critical backend/build/service packages first, verify progress, then add optional toolchains later
If a mirror is flaky, use apt retry behavior or a reliable mirror strategy before changing the project setup approach

problem_signature: Packaged daemons such as Elasticsearch may fail when launched directly as root or without writable data and log directories
symptoms: daemon startup fails with cannot run as root or permission denied
Elasticsearch or another packaged service exits while writing logs, data, pid files, or lock files
raw binary launch fails even though the package installed successfully
root_cause: Many packaged daemons expect to run under a dedicated service user with package-created directories and permissions; launching the raw binary as root bypasses those assumptions.
successful_fix: Prefer the package-provided service wrapper when available
If raw binary launch is necessary, run it as the dedicated service user with su or runuser, without sudo
Before launching, ensure log, data, pid, and config directories are writable by the service user
Inspect daemon logs after a failed start instead of assuming the package install failed

anti_patterns: Do not repeatedly run packaged daemon binaries directly as root after they reject root execution
Do not ignore permission errors under /var/log, /var/lib, or daemon data directories
Do not use sudo inside the container; use service, su, or runuser when needed

problem_signature: Subprocess-based Django tests fail to locate package modules due to missing PYTHONPATH in isolated child processes
symptoms: Subprocess tests fail with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest_django_test' when run via python -m pytest
root_cause: When pytest spawns subprocess tests using sys.executable, it does not automatically inherit the parent process's PYTHONPATH. The child process only sees the system Python path, not the repository root that contains the package.
successful_fix: Set PYTHONPATH=/app explicitly in the environment before running tests: PYTHONPATH=/app python -m pytest tests/
Alternatively, ensure the package is installed in editable mode (pip install -e .) so it's available in site-packages
verification: All 207 tests pass with PYTHONPATH=/app python -m pytest tests/
anti_patterns: Installing the package in non-editable mode alone does not fix subprocess test discovery if setuptools metadata is incomplete
Running pytest without explicitly setting PYTHONPATH when the package is not properly installed will cause subprocess tests to fail

problem_signature: Go build/test fails with 'buildvcs not enabled' error in container environments without git VCS info
symptoms: go build ./... or go test ./... fails with: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
buildvcs not enabled; re-run with -buildvcs=false or set GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false
root_cause: Newer Go versions (1.16+) require git VCS information for builds by default. Container or sandboxed environments often lack a proper git repository context, causing VCS lookup to fail.
successful_fix: Add -buildvcs=false flag to go build and go test commands: go test -buildvcs=false ./...
Alternatively set GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false environment variable globally
verification: go test -buildvcs=false ./... passed successfully
anti_patterns: Attempting to 'fix' the git repository (adding .git directory) is unnecessary and environment-specific
Re-installing Go or downgrading versions is excessive when the flag workaround resolves the issue
embedding_text: Go buildvcs not enabled error container environment git repository. Go 1.16+ requires VCS info by default. Solution: use -buildvcs=false flag with go build/test commands or set GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false environment variable.
